items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: The mention of 'Georgia Tom' appears only in a footnote clarifying the identity of 'Thomas A. Dorsey' mentioned in the interviewee's narration of historical figures (Ma Rainey, etc.). The interviewee does not describe a personal interaction or relationship with Georgia Tom.

ctx.x: Clouds of Joy, Andy Kirk, you know, these guys were the Territory Bands that really, you know, played, but you very rarely saw Duke Ellington in Dallas, you know, during that period. He may play New York or Chicago or the Cotton Club or something and then go to California to Sebastian's or something like that. And then in 1927, when the Regal Theater opened, you know what I mean, they'd have a show. But they always had to have that original TOBA format of a comedian, Pigmeat Markham, you know what I mean,…
*Thomas A. Dorsey, then known as "Georgia Tom." Dorsey went on to compose the popular and well known Gospel hymn, "Precious Lord."
